title: Hobbs v. Massasoit Whip Co.
summary: Retention of eel skins after repeated similar accepted shipments could have contractual significance.
notes:
Casebook discussion of a shorter authority.

Hobbs sought $108.50 for 2,350 skins. Prior dealings gave the recipient reason to act rather than remain silent. The casebook asks what besides mere silence supports the result; the example is not an exception for every unsolicited shipment.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 235–236. Open assigned page 235.
